title: COVID-19 vaccine
what: A vaccine shot in the upper arm that lowers the risk of getting seriously ill with COVID-19.
why: It is now most often advised for older people, those with long-term conditions, pregnant women, and health workers. Ask your doctor if you need it.
duration: the shot takes a few seconds, with the checkup usually 15 to 40 minutes
tell_doctor: If you are ill now or have a fever
When you last had a vaccine or were ill with COVID
Immune system conditions, or treatment that weakens immunity

prepare.title: Health
prepare.text: The vaccine is given when you are well.

prepare.title: Timing
prepare.text: A gap is needed between shots or after illness. Your doctor will say when.

prepare.title: Clothes
prepare.text: Wear something that makes it easy to uncover your upper arm.

steps: The doctor or nurse asks how you feel and takes your temperature
The skin is wiped, and the shot is given
The vaccine is recorded in your documents
After the shot, sit in the clinic for about 30 minutes
feel: Sometimes a sore arm for 1 to 2 days
Sometimes tiredness, a headache, or a fever. It usually passes in 1 to 2 days
after: Stay near the room for 30 minutes
Your doctor will say if another dose is needed
red_flags: Trouble breathing, swelling of the face or throat, or a rash all over: call emergency services
Chest pain, a strong pounding heartbeat, or shortness of breath in the first days after: see a doctor right away

faq.q: Can the vaccine give me COVID?
faq.a: No. The vaccine has no virus that can cause illness.

faq.q: Do I need it if I already had COVID?
faq.a: Sometimes yes, especially in high-risk groups. Your doctor will say when.

reminders.text: COVID-19 vaccine tomorrow. Bring your ID and vaccination certificate.
